title: Economics runtime and optical consolidation

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Approved next-loop runtime and optical correction, frozen defaults, and preservation boundary.
Accepted graph-language refinement for apparent one-pixel strokes, theme-only compensation, terminal axis labels, and stroke-relative arrows.

allowedWork: Economics demand-shift tutorial adapter, local lesson motion projection, retained SVG runtime binding, Graph2D viewport axis marker and label geometry, economics-local CSS/theme tokens, dormant internal appearance controls, focused tests, stable visual evidence, and project/Theseus records.
Preserve and verify the in-scope uncommitted economics corrections already present in the worktree before extending them.
disallowedWork: No semantic economics model changes, lesson prose rewrite, Graph3D implementation, Lisp or other lesson changes, catalogue-wide graph migration, new animation engine, new global salience store, consumer or producer surplus, deadweight loss, or public product work.
Do not stage or modify unrelated user-owned untracked documents or out-of-scope worktree changes.
goal: Restore the economics tutorial to KP's single-clock retained-renderer boundary and establish the reviewed axis, stroke, label, and frozen-default presentation without changing semantic truth.
commitCadence: Commit independently reversible verified groups with exact path staging and completed Theseus evidence; never mix unrelated user-owned files.
stopConditions: Stop at s20 for explicit human review before promotion or generalization.
Stop if semantic economics truth, lesson prose, or publication truth would need to change.
Stop if the unified clock cannot preserve exact direct seek, rewind, URL restoration, and manual-control handoff.
Stop if path conversion changes curve geometry, labels, accessibility, or retained node identity.
Stop if required verification cannot be repaired inside the economics rollback boundary.
Stop if progress would require modifying or staging unrelated dirty files.

slices.title: Recover-and-freeze-baseline
slices.summary: Recovered and froze the canonical two-column dark economics baseline, audited the dirty-worktree boundary, preserved unrelated files, and confirmed 61 semantic/runtime plus 15 stylesheet tests pass before new implementation.

slices.title: Verify-canonical-runtime-ownership
slices.summary: Verified demand already runs on the shared player rAF and retained graph session; isolated the duplicate supply rAF, per-frame Svelte projection feedback, and CSS paint transitions as the three competing authorities. The correction can preserve the semantic asset and stable SVG nodes.

slices.title: Define-unified-lesson-playhead-projection
slices.summary: Added a pure direction-aware lesson playhead projection: the shared player exposes one local normalized clock for either motion block, rewind remains forward-semantic, and the graph receives cumulative demand progress. All 62 focused economics tests pass.

slices.title: Route-supply-motion-through-shared-player
slices.summary: Routed demand shift and supply movement through the one retained editor player; local block playhead and cumulative graph progress now project independently from the same clock, with scroll geometry refreshed after split-layout font settlement.

slices.title: Remove-tutorial-local-playback-clock
slices.summary: Removed the tutorial-local supply rAF, timestamps, cancellation, and playback state. The Svelte lesson adapter now contains no requestAnimationFrame or cancelAnimationFrame authority; the retained editor player owns the only playback clock.

slices.title: Remove-Svelte-frame-feedback-authority
slices.summary: Moved hot-path playback and motion projection into plain runtime objects and a direct retained-DOM presentation adapter. No per-frame Svelte rune drives graph objects or animation-owned CSS; Svelte typecheck passes with zero errors and warnings.

slices.title: Unify-scroll-play-seek-and-URL-drivers
slices.summary: Unified scroll, play, manual scrub, direct semantic links, TOC/history restoration, rewind, and supply handoff through the same local playhead projection. The 12-test tutorial browser suite and 2-test retained runtime session suite pass.

slices.title: Remove-animation-owned-CSS-transitions
slices.summary: Removed CSS interpolation from graph labels, curves, guides, equilibria, axes, and salience paint. Theme and phone UI transitions remain outside animation ownership; the stylesheet contract now rejects graph transition declarations and all 16 CSS tests pass.

slices.title: Prove-retained-renderer-no-op-commit
slices.summary: Added a direct presentation no-op proof: the first retained frame writes its CSS properties and attributes, while committing the identical frame attempts the same projection and performs zero mutations. All 63 focused economics tests pass.

slices.title: Define-path-oriented-data-curve-binding
slices.summary: Defined and tested one path-oriented line-segment contract for economics data curves, explicitly leaving axes, grids, and guide geometry on SVG lines. All 64 focused economics tests pass before caller conversion.

slices.title: Convert-economics-data-curves-to-paths
slices.summary: Converted supply, live demand, both historical-demand layers, and the supply-movement trace from SVG lines to retained paths using the shared d-attribute contract. Axes, grids, and guides remain lines; node identity, direct seek, rewind parity, labels, accessibility, and deterministic static output all pass in 64 unit and 2 browser tests.
